decisions.quote:
We generally confirm H&Q's finding of a high CEO effect, but find a smaller industry effect
and a larger firm effect in our larger sample.
decisions.location: Primary original-specific abstract/discussion comparison; raw source chars[91661,91799), lines1191-1192
decisions.reason: Under the codebook, confirming one specific tested effect is a single comparison rather than an unqualified overall verdict on the replication as a whole, and a tested finding that the paper itself contrasts with the original cannot be left out of the verdict. Throughout the paper (Abstract, Introduction, Section 5.1, Discussion, and Conclusion), the authors compare all variance components of Hambrick and Quigley's (2014) CEO-in-Context (CiC) model in their extended samples against the original results, explicitly contrasting their findings of a much smaller industry effect (0.37% vs. 6.9%) and a larger firm effect (18.65% vs. 12.1%) with their confirmation of a high CEO effect (and further noting that using adjusted R2s markedly reduces the CEO effect). Because the authors explicitly frame their replication results as agreeing on the high CEO effect while differing on the industry and firm effects, the outcome is 'mixed'.
